title: system-words-fold-case-when-akien-types-them
owner: system_word is a tool with users (Law 6): the dispatcher, the base device and shim, and every CLI main call its fold; codemother owns the care of the code (ruling 2026-09-06). CC builds. Each seam's owner gates the two-line write at its address.
intention: Every system word in cairn (a status word, a command word, a marker, any keyword) matches case-insensitively at every seam where the text can come from Akien, with the `cairn` command itself the one lowercase exception.
why: Akien 2026-09-07, answering CC's report that his lowercase 'ruled' had not fired the ruling-intake detector: 'yes. in fact, i suspect all KEYWORDS in cairn should be case insensitive. cairn itself must be lowercase as a command, but everywhere we're talking a status word, or a command word, or any similar 'system word' it should be case insensitive if there's any chance of it coming from me. RULED ruled APPROVED approved Go go GO!' The lived symptom: he types a system word the way his fingers land, and a door that wants the shift key refuses him or stays silent, so a ruling he made by hand had to be recorded by hand.
traces_to: CP4 (design to the tool: the reader here is Akien's fingers, and a keyword that demands his shift key serves itself); Law 1 (a settled answer, 'this word means this verb', re-derived per case is a defect); Law 9 (his lowercase 'ruled' on 2026-09-06 was a measured red at the detector, not a typo to correct); ruling 2026-09-07-system-words-are-case-insensitive-when-akien-types-them (confirmed by his marker in every case). Idea 2026-09-07-yes-in-fact-i-suspect-all-keywords.
falsifier: DONE when test_system_word.py drives the live entry points with mixed-case system words and each behaves as its lowercase form: (1) `cairn RULING LIST` (legacy path) and `cairn HARBOR_MASTER Show MAP Open` (device path) through the real bin/cairn; (2) `cairn Operator SHOW Inbox --SUMMARY`; (3) `cairn review <ID-PREFIX-UPPER>` resolves the berth; (4) `cairn recordverdict APPROVE "..."` resolves the signal; (5) ground_loop `STATUS`; (6) base `_handle_show` with 'MAP' and shim deliver with verb 'SHOW' on a fixture device; (7) a ruling verbatim carrying lowercase 'ruled' confirms at intake and `scan_for_ruling_markers` hits it; (8) the tester CLI accepts `--SEAL`; (9) `bin/cairn` the file and `cairn` the command are untouched. WRONG INTENT if any free-text field (review words, ruling verbatim, learn query, codemother question) is folded, or if a status token stored in a ticket changes case on disk. Horizon: this session.

questions.a: Three load-bearing assumptions, each measured 2026-09-07. (1) Folding collides no two system words: every verb table, view table, learning_block SIGNALS, ground_loop COMMANDS, ruling verbs, skill_block verbs, and every ~/.cairn/devices/*/0/bin/ directory is lowercase-unique. (2) No keyword slot is also a free-text slot: learning_block's `<signal> <words>` vs `<target> <words>` is disambiguated by SIGNALS membership, so folding the membership test and not the stored words keeps his words verbatim; `cairn review <id> "words"` folds only the id prefix. (3) Both ruling matchers read only his text: `ruled_marks` reads the_ruling_verbatim and the hook scans transcript user messages (cli.py:213-217); CC's prose never reaches either.

(a) argparse in the tester CLI is case-sensitive and cannot fold; the build folds argv tokens that start with '-' before parse_args and leaves target paths alone. (b) The bash sites cannot import the python primitive; they fold with `${var,,}` and the proof drives them as subprocesses. Status words typed by him have no live seam today (no CLI takes a stage token), so `clearance.clear` and transitions' target doors fold their target upward as a forward guard; a future CLI that takes a stage word inherits it.
As carried in the falsifier field: nine behavioural teeth over the live entry points plus two wrong-intent teeth (free text verbatim; stored workflow strings untouched). Horizon: this session.

One real collision, settled by the ruling. ruling.py:138 ('UPPERCASE, WORD-BOUNDED, DELIBERATE') and test_ruling.py:286-311 encode that lowercase 'ruled' must NOT confirm. Why of that side: a packet must not confirm on CC's prose. Why of this side: the matchers read only his text, and he ruled with the marker in every case. Exclusive and terminal on the case point; the proof tooth flips and cites decisions/2026-09-07-system-words-are-case-insensitive-when-akien-types-them.json in the same act. Residual accepted by the ruling: 'he ruled that…' in his chat prose raises the hook's one-line report; it never blocks. bin's charter falsifier (1) 'argv is passed verbatim' is a distinction: the dispatcher folds the two tokens it RESOLVES and passes the rest verbatim; the charter gains that sentence.

(a) THE PRIMITIVE — cairn/tools/system_word/system_word.py: `fold(token) -> str` = str(token).strip().casefold(); `is_word(token, *words)`; `pick(token, table)` (fold the key, look up, return value or None); `fold_flags(argv)` (fold only tokens starting with '-'); `fold_head(argv, n)` (fold the first n positional tokens). Charter with gated_by ['CC','Akien'], node_class code-seam. (b) THE SEAMS — bin/cairn: fold device and verb with `${1,,}` before the -x tests, legacy_target likewise; cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin/codemother: `subcmd="${1,,}"`; tools/base/device.py `_handle_get/_handle_show`: pick(what, views); tools/base/shim.py deliver: fold verb before the table test; harbor_master/device.py: fold the filter; machines/ruling/cli.py main: fold verb; ruling.py: RULED = re.compile(r'\bruled\b', re.IGNORECASE), comment carries the ruling; skill_block/__main__.py: fold verb, fold the review id prefix; learning_block/__main__.py: fold argv[0] and the SIGNALS membership tests, keep words verbatim; ground_loop/cli.py: fold cmd; operator_inbox/inbox.py main: fold args[0], target, --summary, the artifact id prefix; orient.py, chart/live.py, librarian/live.py `_main`: fold argv[0]; sudo_relay/daemon.py: fold argv[0]; tester/cli.py: fold_flags before parse_args; transitions target doors and clearance.clear: target.strip().upper(). (c) PROOF — cairn/tools/system_word/proofs/test_system_word.py. (d) RESEALS — every component whose fingerprint moves. (e) CHARTER TOUCHES — bin charter gains the fold sentence; ruling charter gains the ruling; recompile_gate.sh in the same commit. (f) DON'TS — never fold a free-text argument; never rewrite a stored ticket's workflow string; never touch the `cairn` file name; no fold on argparse targets.

constraints: Free text is never folded: review words, ruling verbatim, learn queries, codemother questions, proof target paths pass through byte-identical.
No stored workflow string in any ticket changes case on disk; the fold is at the seam where his text enters, never in the record.
The `cairn` command and the bin/cairn file stay lowercase and untouched in name.
The dispatcher folds only the two tokens it resolves (device, verb) and passes everything else verbatim (bin charter falsifier 1 holds).
The ruling-marker change carries the 2026-09-07 decision in the same act: comment, proof tooth and charter cite it.
how: MEASURED 2026-09-07 at cairn 4a11fcc. Nineteen seams compare a token Akien can type against a system word by bytes: bin/cairn (device, verb, legacy verb); cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin/codemother (`case "$subcmd"`); tools/base/device.py _handle_get/_handle_show (views.get(what)); tools/base/shim.py deliver (verb not in verbs); harbor_master/device.py _filter_fleet (filter_name != 'open'); machines/ruling/cli.py main (verb ==); machines/ruling/ruling.py RULED (r'\bRULED\b', the one strong marker without IGNORECASE); skill_block/__main__.py (verb ==, review id prefix startswith); learning_block/__main__.py (argv[0] ==, args[0] in SIGNALS); ground_loop/cli.py (cmd not in COMMANDS); operator_inbox/inbox.py main (args[0] == 'show', target ==, '--summary' in args, show_artifact prefix); tools/orient/orient.py, skills/chart/live.py, devices/librarian/live.py _main (argv[0] ==); devices/sudo_relay/daemon.py (argv[0] == '--status'); devices/tester/cli.py (argparse flags). THE SEAM: one primitive, cairn/tools/system_word (fold, is_word, pick, fold_flags, fold_head), called at each site in place of the byte compare; bash sites fold with ${var,,}. One proof at the tool drives the real entry points with mixed-case words. The stage-token doors (transitions targets, clearance.clear) fold upward as a forward guard.

intent.what: Every system word in cairn (a status word, a command word, a marker, any keyword) matches case-insensitively at every seam where the text can come from Akien, with the `cairn` command itself the one lowercase exception.

challenge.better_approach: Blanket-lowercase argv in the dispatcher. Rejected: argv carries free text and folding it would alter his verbatim. Per-site .lower() with no primitive. Rejected: the same settled answer written twenty times and nothing to grep for when the next seam appears.
challenge.prior_art: RULING_MARKERS_STRONG already carries re.IGNORECASE on every marker but RULED itself; bash ${var,,} is the folding primitive the dispatcher can use without python. Lab consult (recompiled 2026-09-07): no charter states a case rule for keywords. argparse is case-sensitive by design, so its flags are folded before parse.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That folding never collides two distinct system words (measured: every table and bin/ directory is lowercase-unique). That no keyword slot is also a free-text slot (learning_block disambiguates by SIGNALS membership). That no device bin/ has two entries differing only by case (none).
challenge.real_collision: ruling.py:138 and test_ruling.py:286-311 (lowercase 'ruled' must not confirm) vs this cast. Both matchers read only his text, and he ruled the case rule away with the marker in every case. Exclusive and terminal, settled by the ruling; the tooth flips and cites it.

why_beneath_the_why: A keyword that only matches in one case is a rule the operator has to remember, and a rule remembered is discipline doing physics' job (Law 4). The 2026-08-13 uppercase marker was itself a remembered rule ('I will start saying RULED after every goddamned one'), and it is the one that bit.
